distmer

distance-based mixed-effects models with permutational inference

distmer extends the logic of PERMANOVA into a mixed-model workflow. It uses familiar lmer-style formulas for fixed effects, experimental units, nesting, blocks, repeated observations, and random slopes:

community_distance ~ treatment + (1 | site)

The response is a dissimilarity matrix from vegdist() rather than a single variable. distmer applies a common projection and mixed-design framework to the Gower-centred matrix induced by the user’s chosen dissimilarity (see Anderson 2001). With no random effects, distmer reduces to ordinary PERMANOVA identical to vegan::adonis2(). With a univariate Euclidean response, supported models reduce to their classical stats::anova() or mixed-model counterparts (e.g. lme4::lmer())

fixed effects

The distmer package works directly with distances produced by vegan. The below example uses the pyrifos data to test whether an insecticide (chlorpyrifos) treatment altered aquatic invertebrate community composition:

library(distmer)
library(vegan)

data(pyrifos)

ditch <- gl(12, 1, length = 132)
week  <- gl(11, 12, labels = c(-4, -1, 0.1, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 15, 19, 24))
dose  <- factor(rep(c(0.1, 0, 0, 0.9, 0, 44, 6, 0.1, 44, 0.9, 0, 6), 11))

pyr.env <- data.frame(ditch, week, dose)
pyr.bray <- vegdist(pyrifos)  

fit <- permanova(
  pyr.bray ~ dose,
  data = pyr.env,
  permutations = 999,
  seed = 101
)

summary(fit)

The result reports the ecological effect being tested, its pseudo-(F), permutation p-value, attainable permutation space, and the exchangeability assumptions used for inference.

random effects

For a repeated or grouped field design, add the independent sampling unit in the same way as a mixed-effects model:


fit2 <- permanova(
  pyr.bray ~ dose + (1 | ditch),
  data = pyr.env,
  permutations = 999,
  seed = 101
)

summary(fit2)

dispersion

A location result should be considered alongside multivariate dispersion. The dispersion companion uses the same formula-and-data style:


permanova_dispersion(
   pyr.bray ~ ditch ,
  data = pyr.env,
  permutations = 9999,
  seed = 101
)

Formula:

Ecological question Formula
Do communities differ among groups? d ~ habitat
Does treatment matter after an environmental gradient? d ~ treatment + depth
What is the treatment effect with repeated samples per site? d ~ treatment + (1 \| site)
At which level of a nested survey does an effect occur? d ~ treatment + (1 \| region/site)
Was treatment randomized within blocks? d ~ treatment + (1 \| block) + (1 \| treatment:block)
Do sites differ in their temporal response? d ~ time + (1 + time \| site)

permanova() checks whether the declared design falls inside a validated inference envelope. Unsupported or confounded structures stop with an explanation instead of receiving a convenient but unjustified denominator.

The package also supports planned and pairwise contrasts, multiplicity adjustment, Type I/II/III fixed-effect hypotheses, unbalanced sampling, nested and crossed designs, and validated random-slope models. The guides introduce these in ecological language before exposing implementation details.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github(
  "marine-ecologist/distmer"
)

distmer is currently on the 0.9.0.9000 development line leading to the first stable 1.0.0 release.

vignettes

  1. vignette("getting-started", package = "distmer") — the distance-based mixed-model idea and a first analysis.
  2. vignette("random-effects", package = "distmer") — repeated sites, nested sampling, blocks, hybrids, and random slopes.
  3. vignette("dispersion", package = "distmer") — distance geometry and multivariate dispersion.
  4. vignette("contrasts", package = "distmer") — planned comparisons, pairwise tests, and multiplicity control.
  5. vignette("fixed-effects", package = "distmer") — Type I, II, and III fixed-effect questions.
  6. vignette("unbalanced-mixed", package = "distmer") — unequal cells, missing visits, and unit weighting.
  7. vignette("validation", package = "distmer") — reference agreement, simulations, and reproducible reporting.

Checks:

Supported analyses are tested against vegan, classical scalar analogues, direct matrix calculations, exact permutation enumeration, and adversarial simulation. Distance diagnostics retain and report non-Euclidean geometry rather than silently changing it.

For the detailed evidence and current support boundary, see inst/VALIDATION.md and permanova_capabilities().
